passages.title: Nvidia · Leadership under scrutiny
passages.body: Nvidia's board held urgent discussions about its chief executive after fresh allegations intensified a corporate scandal. Reports of his personal relationships raised questions about governance, and directors considered whether he might be {{2026-11-12-nvidia-ousted}}. Investors reacted sharply, with the company's shares {{2026-11-12-nvidia-plunging}} in after-hours trading. Speculation then turned to the finance chief as a possible {{2026-11-12-nvidia-interim}} leader, although replacing a long-serving founder-like figure would be exceptionally difficult. The uncertainty also {{2026-11-12-nvidia-rattled}} a business central to the artificial-intelligence boom.

passages.title: Chipmakers · A market reshuffle
passages.body: The turbulence at Nvidia gave competing chipmakers an opening in the market. Shares in several American and Chinese rivals {{2026-11-12-chips-surged}} as traders reconsidered which companies might benefit from the upheaval. Meanwhile, a cloud-computing provider that {{2026-11-12-chips-rents}} specialist AI processors reported stronger earnings than analysts had anticipated. Its results {{2026-11-12-chips-beat}} expectations and helped lift sentiment across parts of the technology sector. The divergent moves showed how quickly investors can {{2026-11-12-chips-shift}} their bets within the AI industry.

passages.title: Britain · Growth and inflation risks
passages.body: Britain's economy expanded in the third quarter, {{2026-11-12-britain-bolstered}} by household demand and business spending on artificial intelligence. September's output also increased, despite warnings that higher energy costs were beginning to {{2026-11-12-britain-bite}}. The chancellor cited the figures as evidence of economic {{2026-11-12-britain-resilience}}. Yet the Bank of England had raised interest rates to contain inflation, and analysts worried that tighter credit could {{2026-11-12-britain-weaken}} growth later in the year. The latest figures therefore offered reassurance without eliminating the risks ahead.

passages.title: Europe · Further sanctions on Russia
passages.body: European governments approved another package of restrictions aimed at Russia's financial networks. Officials said the measures would {{2026-11-12-sanctions-target}} banks and other organisations linked to the country's war effort. The wider purpose was to {{2026-11-12-sanctions-disrupt}} financial activity and counter hybrid operations, including misinformation campaigns. France's European-affairs minister said further sanctions would be {{2026-11-12-sanctions-applied}} the following week. The package illustrated the bloc's continuing effort to {{2026-11-12-sanctions-pressure}} Moscow while diplomacy over Ukraine remained uncertain.

passages.title: Spain · Strike and housing anger
passages.body: Millions of workers joined a general strike in Spain, according to labour unions. Demonstrators took to the streets to {{2026-11-12-spain-demand}} action on an increasingly severe housing crisis. Some protests turned confrontational, and clashes {{2026-11-12-spain-broke}} out in major cities. The prime minister had called {{2026-11-12-spain-snap}} elections after parliament failed to pass his proposed housing reforms. The unrest {{2026-11-12-spain-underscored}} how deeply the cost of housing had become entangled with national politics.

passages.title: Ukraine · Connectivity and diplomacy
passages.body: Ukraine's president warned that its armed forces were again experiencing {{2026-11-12-ukraine-patchy}} satellite internet connections. The interruptions were {{2026-11-12-ukraine-hampering}} systems used to intercept hostile drones, adding to pressure on the military. Separately, Russia and Ukraine agreed to a major prisoner {{2026-11-12-ukraine-exchange}}, providing a limited humanitarian opening. American envoys travelled to Moscow to discuss possible terms for peace, although a lasting {{2026-11-12-ukraine-deal}} remained uncertain. The developments highlighted the gap between battlefield difficulties and diplomatic progress.

passages.title: Airlines · Restrictions on AI agents
passages.body: United Airlines announced that personal AI agents would be {{2026-11-12-agents-banned}} from using its online platforms. The company cited the risk of data-privacy {{2026-11-12-agents-violations}} when autonomous software books tickets or checks passengers in. Such third-party bots would therefore be unable to {{2026-11-12-agents-transact}} on travellers' behalf through the airline's systems. Amazon has also {{2026-11-12-agents-restricted}} automated agents on its shopping site, although its leadership has suggested that the policy could change. The decisions reveal growing unease about letting software act independently in commercial transactions.

passages.title: Japan · Matcha supply under strain
passages.body: Global appetite for matcha has risen rapidly, putting Japanese tea producers under {{2026-11-12-matcha-strain}}. Exports have expanded, but ageing farmers are retiring and the industry struggles to keep {{2026-11-12-matcha-pace}} with demand. At an international congress in Tokyo, participants discussed quality standards and the spread of cheap {{2026-11-12-matcha-counterfeits}}. Producers hope that common grading rules will help customers {{2026-11-12-matcha-distinguish}} premium varieties from lower-cost alternatives. The debate reflects the challenge of protecting quality in a fast-growing global market.
